inline.s: What has been spoken above, though it has many expedient means, is all called the wisdom of accordance.

[The three great wondrous gates] Shamatha (stillness), samapatti (equal holding), and dhyana (still contemplation). [Shamatha] Rendered into Chinese as “stillness,” that is, to still one’s thoughts and be aware of the present manifestation of one’s own mind, like a mirror reflecting things. [Samapatti] Rendered into Chinese as “equal holding.” Being free from both dullness and agitation is called “equal”; fixing the mind on a single object is called “holding”; one contemplates the illusory marks and realizes their illusoriness. [Dhyana] Rendered into Chinese as “still contemplation” (stillness and contemplation: stillness is concentration, contemplation is wisdom), also “thought cultivation,” and so on; that is, to be still and quiet the thoughts while contemplating the middle-way principle of “neither empty nor existent, both empty and existent, falling into neither extreme, perfectly fused and unobstructed.”

“Then the Bodhisattva Majestic Power of Freedom, within the assembly, rose from his seat, bowed his head at the Buddha’s feet, circled to the right three times, knelt long with hands clasped, and said to the Buddha: Great compassionate World-Honored One, you have extensively discriminated for us such accordance with the nature of awareness, causing all the bodhisattvas’ minds of awareness to be luminous, and, receiving the Buddha’s perfect voice, they gain the excellent benefit without depending on practice.”

Then, the Bodhisattva Majestic Power of Freedom, within the assembly, rose from his seat, bowed his head at the Buddha’s feet, circled to the right three times, knelt long with hands clasped, and respectfully said to the Buddha: Great compassionate World-Honored One, you have extensively discriminated and set forth these five kinds of accordance with the nature of awareness, causing all the bodhisattvas’ minds of awareness to be luminous, and, receiving the Buddha’s perfect voice, they gain the excellent benefit without depending on practice.
[Perfect voice] The Buddha’s voice is perfect and wonderful; with a single voice he speaks the Dharma, and beings of each type understand it according to their kind.

“World-Honored One, it is like a great city with four gates outside: those who come from each direction do not come by a single road. All the bodhisattvas’ adorning of the buddha-land and attainment of bodhi likewise have not a single expedient means alone. I only pray the World-Honored One to expound extensively for us all the expedient means and the gradual sequences, and how many kinds in all there are of practitioners. May the bodhisattvas of this assembly and the mahayana-seeking sentient beings of the last age quickly attain awakening and sport in the Tathagata’s great sea of quiescent extinction.” Having spoken these words, he prostrated himself with his five limbs on the ground. Three times he made this request, again and again from beginning to end.

World-Honored One, it is like a great city with four gates — east, south, west, and north — outside; those who come from each direction do not come by a single road. All the bodhisattvas’ adorning of the buddha-land and attainment of bodhi are likewise: there is not a single expedient means alone. I only pray the World-Honored One to expound extensively for us all the expedient means and the gradual sequences, and how many kinds in all there are of practitioners. May the bodhisattvas of this assembly and the mahayana-seeking sentient beings of the last age quickly attain awakening and sport in the Tathagata’s great sea of quiescent extinction. The Bodhisattva Majestic Power of Freedom, having spoken these words, prostrated himself with his five limbs on the ground. Three times he made this request, again and again from beginning to end.
[I only pray] “Only” means alone. There is no other wish; it is exclusively for this matter.

“At that time, the World-Honored One said to the Bodhisattva Majestic Power of Freedom: Excellent! Excellent! Good man. You are able, for the sake of all the bodhisattvas and the sentient beings of the last age, to ask the Tathagata about such expedient means. Listen attentively now; I shall speak it for you. At that time, the Bodhisattva Majestic Power of Freedom, receiving the teaching, rejoiced, and the whole assembly listened in silence.”

At that time, the World-Honored One said to the Bodhisattva Majestic Power of Freedom: Excellent! Excellent! Good man. You are able, for the sake of all the bodhisattvas and the sentient beings of the last age, to ask the Tathagata about such expedient means. You may now gather your mind and listen attentively; I shall expound it for you. At that time, the Bodhisattva Majestic Power of Freedom, receiving the teaching, rejoiced, and the whole assembly remained silent and listened.

“Good man! The supreme wonderful awareness pervades the ten directions and gives rise to the Tathagatas and all dharmas, which are one substance and equal. Among all the practices, there is truly no duality. As to the expedient means of accordance, their number is unlimited. Gathering them all together by the way they return, in accordance with the differences of the natures, there should be three kinds.”

Good man! The supreme perfect-enlightened wonderful mind pervades the ten directions and gives rise to the Tathagatas and all dharmas; they are one substance and equal. As to the various methods of practice, there is truly no duality (every dharma is a gate to realization). If one speaks of the expedient means of accordance, their number is unlimited. Gathering them all together, dividing according to the sharpness or dullness of the faculties and the depth of study and practice, there should be three kinds.
[The ten directions] East, south, west, north, southeast, northeast, southwest, northwest, up, and down.
As to the various methods of practice, in substance and in nature there is originally no difference (truly no duality); as to function, there are various differences (their number is unlimited).

“Good man! If bodhisattvas awaken to pure perfect enlightenment, and with the pure aware mind take stillness as practice, then by clearing all thoughts they become aware of the agitation of consciousness. Still wisdom arises, and the guest-dust of body and mind is from then on forever extinguished; then they can internally bring forth stillness and ease. Because of stillness, the minds of all the Tathagatas in the worlds of the ten directions appear within it, like images in a mirror. This expedient means is called shamatha.”

Good man! If bodhisattvas awaken to pure perfect enlightenment (see their own nature), and with the pure aware mind (cultivate in accordance with the nature) observe the still substance of the mind and still their deluded thoughts (take stillness as practice), then by clearing the deluded thoughts (the deluded pondering subsides), they become aware of the agitation of consciousness (they then see the subtle marks of arising and ceasing in the alaya consciousness). Persisting in this, still wisdom arises, and the afflictions of body and mind are from then on forever extinguished; then they can internally bring forth stillness and ease. Because of stillness, the minds of all the Tathagatas in the worlds of the ten directions appear within it, like images in a mirror. This method of practice is called shamatha.

[Take stillness as practice] Taking stillness is to still deluded thoughts in order to purify the present working of the streams of consciousness. [Guest-dust] This refers to afflictions, also called guest-dust afflictions. Afflictions are not inherently possessed by the mind-nature; they arise from being deluded about the principle, hence they are called “guests.” Because they defile the mind-nature, they are called “dust.”

“Good man! If bodhisattvas awaken to pure perfect enlightenment, and with the pure aware mind know that the nature of mind and the faculties and their objects all exist through illusion, then they set up various illusions in order to remove the illusory, and transform various illusions to open the illusory beings. Because of setting up illusion, they can internally bring forth great compassion and ease.”

Good man! If bodhisattvas awaken to pure perfect enlightenment (see their own nature), and with the pure aware mind (cultivate in accordance with the nature) know that the nature of mind and the faculties and their objects all exist through illusion, then they set up illusion-wisdom to contemplate the illusory realm, purifying the present working of the streams of consciousness to remove illusory delusion (purging the fundamental ignorance). (Once ignorance is broken, there is an inconceivable function.) So they transform various illusions and manifest the bodies of the ten realms, in order to reveal and save extensively the illusory beings (living beings). This is because of setting up illusion-wisdom, and so they can internally bring forth great compassion and ease.

This passage explains that after bodhisattvas see their nature (awaken to pure perfect enlightenment), with the pure aware mind they know that the nature of the mind and the faculties and their objects all exist through illusion; so they set up the illusion-contemplation to remove the various illusions, and with various illusory bodies save extensively the illusory beings (transforming various illusions to open the illusory beings).

“All bodhisattvas from this point begin to practice and gradually advance. That which contemplates illusion is not the same as the illusory; yet being not the same as the illusory, the contemplation too is all illusion, so the illusory marks are forever extinguished. The perfect wondrous practice of these bodhisattvas is like a sprout growing in the soil. This expedient means is called samapatti.”

All bodhisattvas from this point begin to practice and gradually advance (dispelling layer by layer: first dispelling the contemplated object, then the contemplating wisdom, until subject and object both vanish and the illusory marks are forever extinguished). That which contemplates illusion (the true wisdom apart from thought) is therefore not the same as the contemplated illusory realm (taking the contemplative as true wisdom and the contemplated as the illusory realm, so one dispels the contemplated realm, keeping only the contemplating wisdom). Although the contemplating wisdom is not the same as the contemplated realm, since both are illusory they must be further dispelled. When subject and object are both extinguished, illusory marks are forever extinguished. The perfect wondrous practice of these bodhisattvas is like a seed in the soil (the buddha-seed) gradually growing into a sprout and a crop. This method of practice is called samapatti.
[That which contemplates illusion is not the same as the illusory] The true wisdom (the one who contemplates illusion) remains alone, and so is not the same as the contemplated illusory realm.

“Good man! If bodhisattvas awaken to pure perfect enlightenment, and with the pure aware mind do not take hold of illusion or the various still marks, understand that body and mind are all hindrances, and without knowledge-awareness and brightness do not rely on the various hindrances; they forever transcend the realm of hindrance and non-hindrance. The world they enjoy, and body and mind, though their marks are within the realm of dust, are like the sound within a vessel: the sound comes forth beyond it. Afflictions and nirvana do not obstruct each other.”

Good man! If bodhisattvas awaken to pure perfect enlightenment (see their own nature), and with the pure aware mind (cultivate in accordance with their nature) do not take hold of illusion or the various still marks, and know that body and mind are all hindrances; without knowledge-awareness brightness (apart from thought), they do not rely on the various hindrances of body and mind, and forever transcend the realm of hindrance and non-hindrance. Though the marks of the world they enjoy and of body and mind are within the realm of dust, the dharma-body far surpasses the realm of dust (as the sound of a bell or drum lies far beyond the bell and drum themselves); afflictions and nirvana each do not obstruct the other.

[Knowledge-awareness brightness] The brightness of knowledge-awareness. The Surangama Sutra says: “When knowing and seeing establish a knowing, that is the root of ignorance; when knowing and seeing do not see, that is nirvana.” Knowledge-awareness brightness is the established knowing, which is the root of ignorance. [A sound within a vessel] “Vessel” refers to a musical instrument, the bell or drum; “sound” is a loud, resonant note. [Like the sound within a vessel, the sound comes forth beyond it] Like the sound of a bell or drum, which lies far beyond the bell and drum themselves.

“Then they can internally bring forth quiescent-extinction ease, the wonderful awareness in accordance. The realm of quiescent extinction is beyond the reach of one’s own and others’ body and mind; the lifespans of living beings are all floating thoughts. This expedient means is called dhyana.”

Then they can internally bring forth quiescent-extinction ease, the wonderful awareness in accordance. This realm of quiescent extinction is beyond the reach of one’s own and others’ body and mind; the lifespans of living beings are all floating thoughts. This method of practice is called dhyana.

“Good man! These three dharma-gates are all close accordance with perfect enlightenment. The Tathagatas of the ten directions become buddhas because of these. The various expedient means of the bodhisattvas of the ten directions, all that are alike and all that are different, all rely on these three kinds of work; if one perfectly realizes them, one attains perfect enlightenment.”

Good man! These three great dharma-gates are all methods of practice that closely accord with perfect enlightenment. The Tathagatas of the ten directions all become buddhas through practicing these gates. The bodhisattvas of the ten directions, with their various expedient means, whether alike or different (practicing one of the three gates, or two, or all three, and so on — see the “twenty-five wheels” of the next chapter), in substance all rely on these three great gates; if one perfectly realizes them, one attains perfect enlightenment.

[The various expedient means of the bodhisattvas of the ten directions, all alike and all different, all rely on these three kinds of work] The bodhisattvas of the worlds of the ten directions have various methods of practice; among them there are those that are alike (same) and those that are different (different), but in substance they all rely on these three great dharma-gates.

“Good man! Suppose a person cultivates the holy path and teaches living beings to accomplish the fruits of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of arhats and pratyekabuddhas; this is not equal to a person who hears this unimpeded dharma-gate of perfect enlightenment and, in a single instant, accords with it in practice.”

Good man! Suppose a person cultivates the holy path and teaches living beings to accomplish the fruits of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of arhats and pratyekabuddhas; it is not equal to a person who hears this unimpeded dharma-gate of perfect enlightenment and, in a single instant, accords with it in practice.

“O Majestic, you should know: the mind of supreme great awareness, in its original limit, has no two marks. According with the various expedient means, their number is indeed unlimited. The Tathagata, in his overall instruction, sets forth three kinds: stillness, that is shamatha, like a mirror reflecting the various images; illusion-like, that is samapatti, like a sprout gradually growing; and dhyana alone, quiescent extinction, like the sound within a vessel.”

O Majestic, you should know: the mind of supreme perfect enlightenment, in its original limit, has no two marks. According with the various expedient means, there is an unlimited number. The Tathagata, in his overall instruction, sets forth three great wondrous gates: taking stillness, shamatha, like a mirror reflecting the various images (faithfully manifesting them); the illusion-contemplation, samapatti, like a sprout gradually growing (when illusion is exhausted, truth appears); and dhyana alone, still contemplation, like the sound within a vessel (far surpassing the various hindrances).

“These three wonderful dharma-gates are all the accordance of awareness. The Tathagatas of the ten directions and the great bodhisattvas attain the Way because of them. Because the three are perfectly realized, it is called ultimate nirvana.”

These three wonderful dharma-gates are all the accordance of perfect enlightenment. The Tathagatas of the ten directions and the great bodhisattvas attain the Way because of them. Because the three are perfectly realized, it is called ultimate nirvana.

[The twenty-five wheels] This is the various combinations and arrangements of the three great wondrous gates (shamatha, samapatti, and dhyana): taking one of the three, or two, or all three, plus differences in their order of sequence — altogether twenty-five kinds.

“Then the Bodhisattva Distinguishing Sound, within the assembly, rose from his seat, bowed his head at the Buddha’s feet, circled to the right three times, knelt long with hands clasped, and said to the Buddha: Great compassionate World-Honored One, such dharma-gates are exceedingly rare. World-Honored One, as to these expedient means, of all the bodhisattvas within the gate of perfect enlightenment, how many kinds of practice are there? I pray that, for the sake of the assembly and the sentient beings of the last age, you reveal them by expedient means, causing them to awaken to the reality of all dharmas.” Having spoken these words, he prostrated himself with his five limbs on the ground. Three times he made this request, again and again from beginning to end.

Then, the Bodhisattva Distinguishing Sound, within the assembly, rose from his seat, bowed his head at the Buddha’s feet, circled to the right three times, knelt long with hands clasped, and respectfully said to the Buddha: Great compassionate World-Honored One, such three great dharma-gates are exceedingly rare. World-Honored One, as to these methods of practice, of all the bodhisattvas within the gate of perfect enlightenment, how many modes of practice are there? I pray that, for the sake of the assembly and the sentient beings of the last age, you reveal them by expedient means, causing them to awaken to the reality of all dharmas. The Bodhisattva Distinguishing Sound, having spoken these words, prostrated himself with his five limbs on the ground. Three times he made this request, again and again from beginning to end.

“At that time, the World-Honored One said to the Bodhisattva Distinguishing Sound: Excellent! Excellent! Good man. You are able, for the sake of the great assembly and the sentient beings of the last age, to ask the Tathagata about such practice. Listen attentively now; I shall speak it for you. At that time, the Bodhisattva Distinguishing Sound, receiving the teaching, rejoiced, and the whole assembly listened in silence.”

At that time, the World-Honored One said to the Bodhisattva Distinguishing Sound: Excellent! Excellent! Good man. You are able, for the sake of all the bodhisattvas and the sentient beings of the last age, to ask the Tathagata about the practice of these three great wondrous gates. You may now gather your mind and listen attentively; I shall expound it for you. At that time, the Bodhisattva Distinguishing Sound, receiving the teaching, rejoiced, and the whole assembly remained silent and listened.

“Good man! The perfect enlightenment of all the Tathagatas is pure and pristine; originally there is no practice and no one who practices. All the bodhisattvas and the sentient beings of the last age, relying on not-yet-awareness, practice through an illusory power; at that time there are twenty-five kinds of pure concentration wheels:”

Good man! The perfect enlightenment of all the Tathagatas is pure and pristine; originally there is no practice and no one who practices. All the bodhisattvas and the sentient beings of the last age, relying on not-yet-awareness, practice through an illusory power; at that time there are twenty-five kinds of pure types:

“If bodhisattvas take only extreme stillness, and because of the power of stillness forever sever afflictions and accomplish the ultimate, without rising from the seat enter nirvana — these bodhisattvas are said to practice shamatha alone.”

If bodhisattvas take only extreme stillness, and because of the power of stillness forever sever afflictions and accomplish the ultimate, without rising from the seat enter nirvana — the method of these bodhisattvas is called practicing shamatha alone.

“If bodhisattvas contemplate only the illusion-like, and because of the power of the Buddha transform the world’s various operations, fully practicing the pure and wondrous conduct of a bodhisattva, and in the dharani do not lose the still thought and the various still wisdoms — these bodhisattvas are said to practice samapatti alone.”

If bodhisattvas contemplate only the illusion-like, and because of the power of the Buddha transform the world’s various operations, fully carrying out the bodhisattva’s various pure and wondrous conducts, and in the dharani (the total-holding) do not lose the still thought and the various still wisdoms — the method of these bodhisattvas is called practicing samapatti alone.

“If bodhisattvas only extinguish the various illusions, not taking up any operation, alone severing afflictions, and when afflictions are completely severed then realize the reality of all dharmas — these bodhisattvas are said to practice dhyana alone.”
